response.sql:
WITH customer_orders AS (
    SELECT c.customer_id,
           c.gender,
           COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count
    FROM Customers AS c
    JOIN Orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
    WHERE c.gender IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.gender
), shares AS (
    SELECT customer_id,
           gender,
           order_count,
           CAST(order_count AS DECIMAL(38, 18))
               / SUM(order_count) OVER (PARTITION BY gender) AS share
    FROM customer_orders
), gaps AS (
    SELECT customer_id,
           gender,
           order_count,
           share,
           share - AVG(share) OVER () AS above_average
    FROM shares
)
SELECT customer_id,
       gender,
       order_count,
       share,
       above_average
FROM gaps
WHERE above_average > 0
ORDER BY CASE WHEN above_average IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END,
         above_average DESC
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: Treat a missing gender as SQL NULL and exclude those customers. “Average share across these customers” means the unweighted arithmetic mean of individual customer shares across all genders. The share uses exact decimal arithmetic with a fixed scale of 18 decimal places, so it is not rounded but may be truncated by the database’s decimal type.
